text:
A smarter way to
understand weather
Live forecasts, practical recommendations, and a personal weather profile in one focused experience.

Introduce SkyCast as a weather application that turns live forecast data into practical daily planning. Mention that the project combines a React interface, external weather services, authentication, and a Supabase data layer.
Weather apps often show the data. Users still have to decide what it means for their day.
Forecasts, maps, and saved places live in separate moments.
Temperature alone does not tell a user when an activity will feel comfortable.
A useful answer depends on location, preferences, and the user’s plans.

“Is this weather
right for my plans?”
A decision, not just a forecast
Explain that the project focuses on the gap between weather data and everyday decisions. Users need context, not only a list of measurements.
SkyCast brings the forecast, the decision, and the personal profile into one place.
Activity suggestions based on the forecast
Saved places and preferences that stay with the user
Present SkyCast as a connected product. The application combines live weather information, practical recommendations, and persistence through a user profile.
The flow stays short: choose a place, understand the forecast, then act on it.
Search for a city or use current location
Read current, hourly, and daily conditions
See the best time for activities
Keep places and preferences in the profile
Walk through the journey in four steps. The interface avoids unnecessary screens and keeps the user focused on the next useful decision.
The first screen answers the most important question: what is happening now, and what comes next?
Use this slide to explain the dashboard hierarchy. The current condition is prominent, while supporting metrics and the next hours remain visible without opening another screen.
SkyCast translates weather conditions into simple recommendations for the day.
Emphasize the practical value of the activity cards. The recommendations make the weather forecast easier to use in everyday life.
Users can search for a city, use their current location, compare destinations, and see the result on a map.
Search results stay connected to the forecast
Explain how location search and comparison help users make decisions before travelling or choosing between two places.
The assistant turns weather data into answers that match the user’s question.
Is the weather good for a walk?
Yes. Choose a cooler time and check rain.
Users can ask about walks, rain, locations, and timing.
Answers use the selected location and current forecast.
The app can still provide a local answer when the AI service is unavailable.
Describe the assistant as a conversational layer on top of the weather data. Give one example question and explain that the answer uses the selected location and forecast context.
A signed-in user keeps the places and settings that make SkyCast useful over time.
Meaningful actions linked to the user
Explain that authentication makes the experience personal. The profile stores saved places, display preferences, and activity records so the user can return to the same setup later.
Supabase provides authentication, secure storage, and user-level data access.

Email and password
Identity and session
Every row is linked to one user
Explain the three application tables. Authentication identifies the user, while the public tables store only the profile data, saved places, and activity records needed by the application.
The application combines a React client with weather services, location services, and Supabase.
Leaflet map  ·  Nominatim geocoding  ·  Optional AI chat service
Describe how the parts work together. React handles the interface, Open-Meteo provides forecast information, and Supabase manages identity and persistent user data.
The database protects user-owned data through authentication and Row Level Security.
Only signed-in users can access profile data.
Policies restrict each record to its owner.
The frontend uses a publishable key, never a service-role secret.
Profile creation runs through a restricted database function.
Explain that the design separates authentication from application data and uses Row Level Security to prevent one user from reading another user’s records.
The main user flows and the production build were checked before delivery.
Search results select a new location
Saved places add and remove correctly
Sign in and account creation UI
Profiles and preferences sync with Supabase
Summarize the validation work. The application was checked for the main interaction flows, database structure, responsive layout, and successful production compilation.
The current foundation supports a broader personal weather planning experience.
Trends across saved places and activities
More activity types and richer recommendations
Share a weather plan with friends
Present these as realistic extensions rather than commitments. The existing authentication, profile, and weather foundation makes each direction feasible.

Weather information
that helps people plan.
Live forecasts, useful recommendations, and a profile that remembers what matters.
Close by restating the product value: SkyCast turns weather information into better daily decisions. Invite questions about the user experience, architecture, or database design.
